description:
Upper plan view (standard geometry, no view title printed): A triangular raised island with integral curb and gutter and 2 ft radius (R=2', TYP) corners separates the right turn lane from the through lanes on the left. A marked crosswalk crosses the through lanes at the left and another crosses the turn lane at the right. A pedestrian cut-through passes through the island, with a 48 in landing (typical, at top of all curb ramps, see Note 2) and 2% MAX slope arrows at the landing and cut-through. Dimensions on the island: 2' MIN. offset between the crosswalk and the island, 5' MIN. island width at the top, a 5' MIN. cut-through dimension, and 4' MIN on both sides (path width each side). A callout reads: if more than 9 ft wide, install bollard(s) in the detectable warning surface (DWS) at 2 ft maximum from the flow line, allowing a minimum of 4 ft path in between bollards. The island edge along the turn lane is 20' MIN. long and meets the approach at 55 to 70 degrees. The turn lane is 11' MIN., 14' MAX. wide (see Note 1). A 2% TYP, 5% MAX label marks the cross slope on the turn lane side. A unidirectional curb ramp without flares (TYP, see S-442) serves the island and a parallel curb ramp (see S-442) serves the corner. The outside curb has integral curb and gutter and a corner radius R=25' to 40' (see corner radius policy). The turn lane curb has integral curb and gutter at R=150' to 275'. Pavement arrows show the right turn and through movements.

Lower plan view, titled 'Constrained Geometric Design for Channelized Right Turns' with the title block line 'Right Angle Approach': Same layout at a corner with a narrow sidewalk (9 ft or less, labeled 'Narrow sidewalk (<=9')'). The island is a narrow triangle with integral curb and gutter and R=2', TYP, 48 in landing (typical at top of all curb ramps, see Note 2), a curb ramp (TYP, see S-442) at the island, and 2' MIN. offsets at the crosswalks. The island edge is 20' MIN. long at 55 to 70 degrees to the approach. The turn lane is 11' MIN., 14' MAX. (see Note 1) with 2% TYP and 5% MAX cross slope noted. A parallel curb ramp (see S-442) is shown at the corner on the narrow sidewalk. Curbs are integral curb and gutter at R=150' to 275' on the turn lane side. Arrows show a left turn on the through street and a right turn on the slip lane.

Title block: SUPPLEMENTAL DESIGN GUIDE, Detail 100, Sheet 1 of 2. A file stamp along the left margin gives the source drawing name 'Right Turn Slip Lane - BOE2.dwg' dated 4/2/2020.

title: Geometric Design for Channelized Right Turns, Right Angle Approach (Detail 100, Sheet 1 of 2)
summary: Supplemental Design Guide Detail 100, sheet 1 of 2, shows two plan views of a channelized right turn at a right angle approach: a standard geometry and a constrained geometry with a narrow sidewalk (9 ft or less). Key values are a 55 to 70 degree island approach angle, a 20 ft minimum island length, an 11 to 14 ft turn lane, a 25 to 40 ft corner radius and a 150 to 275 ft turn lane radius. Pedestrian landings are 48 in with 2% maximum slope and curb ramps follow S-442.

description:
Plan view, titled 'Unconstrained Geometric Design for Channelized Right Turns': A bike lane crossing and a pedestrian crossing are shown side by side across the top leg, with a 3' MIN separation between them. At the left a crosswalk crosses the through lanes. A pedestrian and bicyclist island sits between the through lanes and the turn lane, with detectable warning surface (DWS) at the crossings, 6' MIN. island width, 4' MIN on both sides, and section cut A (sheet 2) through the island at the top crossing. A non-walkable surface, raised divisional island or curbing (TYP) edges the island with 5' MIN and 8' MIN dimensions at the island ends, R=5' MIN at a corner and R=10' MIN at the sidewalk side corner. Unidirectional curb ramps without flares (TYP, see S-442) serve the crossings, with a 4' MIN dimension at the corner island. Turning geometry: 11' MIN., 14' MAX. turn lane (see Note 1), integral curb and gutter R=2' TYP at the tip of the island, a 55 to 70 degree island approach angle, a 20' MIN. island length, outer corner radius R=25' to 40' (see corner radius policy), and 150' to 275' radius on the turn lane curb. Beyond the turn lane the plan shows, from the road outward, a grass buffer, a bike lane and a sidewalk. An optional raised crosswalk and bike crossing is called out as 'see Supplemental Design Guide Detail 600'.

Section A, 'Typical Section A at Pedestrian/Bicyclist Island', subtitle 'Steep Road Cross Slopes' (cut A on sheet 2): Left to right: repair or reconstruct street paving as necessary, 2' MIN, TYP, sloping to integral curb and gutter TYP; a 6' MIN. non-walkable surface (hatched) bounded by a curb; an 8' MIN. bike lane between a battered curb without gutter (TYP, see Supplemental Design Guide Detail 400) and a second battered curb; a 3' non-walkable surface (hatched) between battered curbs; then a 3' warning curb; a sidewalk curb ramp; a variable width island; and an integral curb and gutter beside the right turn lane with a break line.

description:
Option 1 plan view: A street corner with sidewalk (concrete) and two curb ramps (SEE S-442, see Note 6), one on each leg. On each leg the curb bulbs out with R=25' reverse curves (see Note 5). The extension is 4' MIN TO 8' MAX (see Note 3) wide measured from the existing curb and its length is 'varies (Note 4)' for the transition. A 24" MIN. dimension sets the offset between the crosswalk side of the ramp and the start of the extension on each leg. The area behind the new curb is a paved or vegetated area (see Notes 1 and 2) shown stippled. The sidewalk width 'varies'. Section cuts A1 (sheet 3) and A2 (sheet 4) are marked across the extension on the left leg. On the right leg a break line shows the extension runs into the gutter with a 'new side opening catch basin 20' away from the curb extension' and an 'assumed drainage flow' arrow along the gutter.

Option 2 plan view: Same corner geometry, with the extension configured as a non-walkable paved or vegetated area (see Notes 1 and 2) along the curb (TYP non-walkable surface), with a curb ramp (see S-442, Note 6) in line with the crosswalks. Dimensions: R=25' (Note 5), 4' MIN TO 8' MAX curb extension (Note 3), 'varies' transition length (Note 4), 'varies' sidewalk. Section cut B (sheet 4) is marked on the left leg. A new side opening catch basin is placed 20' away from the curb extension with assumed drainage flow arrow.

Two corner islands are drawn: one on each approach leg, separated from the corner by a bike lane. Each island has R=25' (see Notes 5 and 22) outer curve, R=2' corners, R=1' (TYP, see Note 20) small corners on the pedestrian islands, 9' MIN width and 5' MIN bike lane width at the right, and 24" MIN. gaps. At the left, a truck apron (see Supplemental Design Guide Detail 300) with R=2' (TYP) and R=5' corners lies next to a 6' MIN pedestrian cut-through with 6' MAX and 6' MIN dimensions. Detectable warning surface cut-through is 9' MIN wide, with the callout: if more than 9 ft wide, install bollard(s) in the DWS at 2' maximum from the flow line, allowing a minimum of 4' path in between bollards. A bike lane runs along the curb. Section cuts G1 and G2 (sheet 10) are marked on the two legs. Labels: curb, varies existing parkway or paving (see Note 3).

Section G1, 'Typical Section for Type 2 Protected Intersection with Existing Curb and Gutter': Left to right: existing sidewalk or ground; existing curb and gutter (see Note 11); a 4' MIN bike lane (exclusive of gutter), hatched; battered curb w/o gutter (see Supplemental Design Guide Detail 400); a 9' MIN concrete or asphalt island slab over existing roadway to be removed; integral curb (see Notes 14 and 22); repair or reconstruct street paving as necessary, 2' MIN, typical (see Note 7).

Section G2, 'Typical Section for Type 2 Protected Intersection with Rebuilt Curb and Gutter': Left to right: existing sidewalk or ground; existing curb and gutter to be removed; a 5' MIN bike lane (extend gutter) on new integral curb and gutter across full width of bike lane; battered curb w/o gutter (see Supplemental Design Guide Detail 400); a 9' MIN concrete or asphalt island slab over existing roadway to be removed; integral curb (see Notes 14 and 22); repair or reconstruct street paving as necessary, 2' MIN (see Note 7).

description: Notes sheet: The sheet contains only the heading 'NOTES' and 22 numbered notes in a single column, with no drawing. The notes apply to the curb extension views, sections and layouts on sheets 1 to 10 of Detail 200 and refer to Standard Plans S-311, S-320, S-322, S-410, S-430, S-432, S-442, S-480, S-484 and DL-2327. Title block: SUPPLEMENTAL DESIGN GUIDE, Detail 200, Sheet 11 of 11. File stamp: Curb Extensions_BOE_DOT2.dwg, 4/2/2020.
notes:
NOTES
1. See Standard Plan S-484 for details involving vegetated stormwater curb extensions, which may be used for situations involving landscaped areas within a non-walkable area.
2. Area shall be paved and adhere to Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) requirements when walkable slopes can be achieved. When walkable slopes are unattainable, treatments shall be installed to discourage pedestrians from walking in the area. Non-walkable alternatives include vegetation as shown in Standard Plan S-484, raised planting beds, or flush planting beds with a valley gutter. See cross sections A-1 for details on alternatives. Inlets may also be provided within the non-walkable areas and curb openings may be provided in the warning curb to allow runoff in the sidewalk to reach these inlets.
3. Where structurally feasible and no parkway obstructions interfere or require curb for lateral support, width of Type 1 curb extension shall remove existing curb and gutter to incorporate the adjacent parkway and follow Section A-1. Otherwise the typical section minimum width is 3'-6" from inside existing and new curbs.
4. Transition length shall vary based the width of the curb extension and the curb radii used for the transition. (Printed as 'based the width'.)
5. A street side curb radius of 25' is required for completed street sweeping from gutter to face of curb. A curb radius of 10 feet is allowable to increase area of the storage/detention area only if the adjacent property owner assumes full responsibility for any gutter maintenance as may be required due to lack of street sweeping.
6. See Standard Plan S-442 for details involving curb ramps. Choose curb ramp to fit conditions. Where curb extension has reverse slope, ramp slope shall not be less than 2% toward the street.
7. Modify the existing street paving as necessary to restore a smooth transition and street crown (Standard Plan S-432, similar). Match paving materials and thickness, see S-410 for standard curbs & gutters. Ensure positive drainage is provided.
8. Construct concrete sidewalk when specified on plan. Sidewalk minimum clearance 60".
9. All concrete & sidewalks shall be Class 520-C-2500 Portland cement concrete. Install contraction, expansion and weakened plane joints in concrete per S-480 & S-430.
10. Minimum relative compaction of earthwork under new paving shall be per SSPWC. See S-480 for further requirements.
11. Existing curb height generally varies from 5 inches to 8 inches.
12. A walkable alternative is the preferred option when ADA compliant grades can be achieved. Factors affecting the ability to produce walkable grades include the roadway cross slope, existing curb height, existing ground or sidewalk elevation, and the width of the sidewalk extension. Slopes not to exceed 2%.
13. Where grades can be modified, Type C curb and gutter with a standard curb height shall be installed. New curb may be installed with a curb height between 5 to 8 inches to create walkable slopes on the curb extension. Where approved by Bureau of Engineering, a Type C (modified) depressed curb and gutter may be utilized if a reduced curb height produces a walkable slope of 2% or less. Curb heights less than 5" require approval of City Engineer.
14. Overall curb height will vary based on existing grades and curb reveals. Ensure that curb depth extends at least 8 inches below finished grade.
15. The inlet and outlet shall be designed per Standard Plan S-322 (steel) or Standard Plan DL-2327 (concrete) depending on the culvert top material. The inlet opening shall be at least as wide as the culvert, but may be wider based on the hydraulic analysis (check spread during the design storm).
16. Warping the gutter (per Std Plan S-311) is optional, which will result in a lower elevation at Point A, effecting the longitudinal slope (see Note #3).
17. The curb ramp landing shall adhere to Standard Plan S-442. The culvert top shall be slip resistant and ADA compliant.
18. The culvert top shall be either concrete (per Std Plan S-320 and DL-2327), steel (per Std Plan S-322), or grated (as approved by BOE). A maintenance hole lid may optionally be installed along the length of the culvert when the top is concrete. A concrete culvert top will result in a lower elevation at Point A, effecting the longitudinal slope (see Note #3). A maintenance agreement shall be in place prior to the installation of culvert.
19. The minimum inside width of the culvert is 2 feet. At the discretion of the office engineer, the absolute minimum width that is permitted is 1.5 feet. A narrower width may be necessary to construct the curb ramp.
20. A 2 foot typical curb radius is preferred for all island corners. A 1 foot radius or squared corners may be used to maximize the footprint and improve constructability of islands less than 10 square feet in size.
21. Valleys created from reverse slopes shall be drained back to the curb when possible to avoid ponding on the curb extension. The use of a valley gutter requires the approval of the City Engineer. Where a cross slope of 2% or less is not feasible, a non-walkable surface must be provided.
22. Where drainage is a concern as instructed by the City Engineer, Type C curb & gutter shall be installed.
